1: //! # Incomplete Analysis: Linter-Internal Limit Checks
2: //!
3: //! This module implements the 17 "Incomplete Analysis" checks from MATLAB's Code
4: //! Analyzer. These are special internal-limit diagnostics that **cannot be disabled**
5: //! by the user. They all have default severity `Error`.
6: //!
7: //! ## Check IDs
8: //!
9: //! | Check ID | Description                                  | Detection                                  |
10: //! |----------|----------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
11: //! | TMMSG    | More than 10,000 diagnostics generated       | Post-lint (diagnostic count > threshold)   |
12: //! | TMSMS    | More than 1,000 parse errors generated       | Count ERROR nodes in tree                  |
13: //! | MXASET   | File too complex to analyze                  | Node count > threshold                     |
14: //! | QUIT     | Analysis did not complete                    | Engine panic guard (`catch_unwind` in `Linter::lint`) |
15: //! | NOSPC    | File too complex (nesting)                   | Max nesting depth > threshold              |
16: //! | MBIG     | File too large                               | Source length > threshold                  |
17: //! | NOFIL    | File not found                               | No-op (handled by CLI)                     |
18: //! | MDOTM    | Invalid file extension                       | File extension != `.m`                     |
19: //! | MDMCR    | Deployed MATLAB file                         | File extension == `.ctf` or `.p`           |
20: //! | RDERR    | Unable to read file                          | No-op (handled by CLI)                     |
21: //! | EOFER    | Too many syntax errors                       | ERROR node count > threshold               |
22: //! | EOFMI    | Incomplete file                              | Last node is ERROR or MISSING              |
23: //! | MDEEP    | Parentheses/brackets nested too deeply       | Max `()`, `[]`, `{}` nesting depth         |
24: //! | DEEPC    | Block comments nested too deeply             | Nested `%{ %}` detection                   |
25: //! | DEEPN    | Functions nested too deeply                  | Nested `function_definition` depth         |
26: //! | DEEPS    | Statements nested too deeply                 | Nested if/for/while/switch/try depth       |
27: //! | TEXTL    | Text too long                                | Max line length > threshold                |
28: //!
29: //! ## Configuration
30: //!
31: //! ```toml
32: //! [lint.rules.INCOMPLETE_ANALYSIS]
33: //! max_diagnostics = 10000
34: //! max_parse_errors = 1000
35: //! max_node_count = 100000
36: //! max_file_size = 1048576
37: //! max_paren_depth = 32
38: //! max_function_depth = 20
39: //! max_statement_depth = 15
40: //! max_line_length = 4096
41: //! ```

158: /// Incomplete Analysis Engine: a file-level rule that handles all 17
159: /// incomplete-analysis checks in a single pass.
160: ///
161: /// These checks represent linter-internal limits and cannot be disabled
162: /// by the user (`can_be_disabled() == false`).
163: pub struct IncompleteAnalysisEngine {
164:     config: IncompleteAnalysisConfig,
165: }
166: 
167: impl IncompleteAnalysisEngine {
168:     /// Factory constructor. Reads rule-specific params from config.
169:     pub fn from_config(config: &Config) -> Box<dyn Rule> {
170:         let rule_config: IncompleteAnalysisConfig = config.rule_params("INCOMPLETE_ANALYSIS");
171:         Box::new(Self {
172:             config: rule_config,
173:         })
174:     }
175: 
176:     /// Walk the tree and collect all metrics in one pass.
177:     fn collect_metrics(&self, root: Node) -> TreeMetrics {
178:         let mut metrics = TreeMetrics::default();
179: 
180:         // Check last child of root for EOFMI.
181:         if let Some(last) = last_descendant(root) {
182:             metrics.last_node_is_error = last.is_error() || last.is_missing();
183:         }
184: 
185:         Self::walk_tree(root, &mut metrics, 0, 0, 0);
186:         metrics
187:     }
188: 
189:     /// Recursive DFS traversal that collects node counts, error counts, and
190:     /// nesting depths in a single pass.
191:     fn walk_tree(
192:         node: Node,
193:         metrics: &mut TreeMetrics,
194:         paren_depth: usize,
195:         function_depth: usize,
196:         statement_depth: usize,
197:     ) {
198:         metrics.node_count += 1;
199: 
200:         if node.is_error() {
201:             metrics.error_count += 1;
202:         }
203: 
204:         // Track parentheses/bracket nesting depth (MDEEP).
205:         let new_paren_depth = match node.kind() {
206:             "parenthesis" | "arguments" | "matrix" | "cell" => {
207:                 let d = paren_depth + 1;
208:                 if d > metrics.max_paren_depth {
209:                     metrics.max_paren_depth = d;
210:                 }
211:                 d
212:             }
213:             _ => paren_depth,
214:         };
215: 
216:         // Track function nesting depth (DEEPN).
217:         let new_function_depth = if node.kind() == "function_definition" {
218:             let d = function_depth + 1;
219:             if d > metrics.max_function_depth {
220:                 metrics.max_function_depth = d;
221:             }
222:             d
223:         } else {
224:             function_depth
225:         };
226: 
227:         // Track statement nesting depth (DEEPS).
228:         let new_statement_depth = match node.kind() {
229:             "if_statement" | "for_statement" | "while_statement" | "switch_statement"
230:             | "try_statement" => {
231:                 let d = statement_depth + 1;
232:                 if d > metrics.max_statement_depth {
233:                     metrics.max_statement_depth = d;
234:                 }
235:                 d
236:             }
237:             _ => statement_depth,
238:         };
239: 
240:         // Recurse into children.
241:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
242:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
243:             Self::walk_tree(
244:                 child,
245:                 metrics,
246:                 new_paren_depth,
247:                 new_function_depth,
248:                 new_statement_depth,
249:             );
250:         }
251:     }
252: 
253:     /// Check maximum line length (TEXTL).
254:     fn check_line_lengths(&self, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
255:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
256:         let mut byte_offset = 0;
257: 
258:         for (line_idx, line) in source.lines().enumerate() {
259:             let char_len = line.chars().count();
260:             if char_len > self.config.max_line_length {
261:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
262:                     rule_id: "TEXTL",
263:                     message: format!(
264:                         "Line length ({char_len}) exceeds internal limit ({max})",
265:                         max = self.config.max_line_length
266:                     ),
267:                     severity: Severity::Error,
268:                     byte_range: byte_offset..byte_offset + line.len(),
269:                     line: line_idx + 1,
270:                     column: 1,
271:                     fix: None,
272:                 });
273:             }
274:             // +1 for newline character.
275:             byte_offset += line.len() + 1;
276:         }
277: 
278:         diagnostics
279:     }
280: 
281:     /// Scan source text for nested block comments (DEEPC).
282:     ///
283:     /// MATLAB block comments are `%{ ... %}`. Nesting is not allowed — a
284:     /// second `%{` inside an open block comment is an error.
285:     fn check_nested_block_comments(&self, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
286:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
287:         let mut depth: usize = 0;
288:         let mut byte_offset = 0;
289: 
290:         for (line_idx, line) in source.lines().enumerate() {
291:             let trimmed = line.trim();
292:             if trimmed == "%{" {
293:                 depth += 1;
294:                 if depth > 1 {
295:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
296:                         rule_id: "DEEPC",
297:                         message: format!(
298:                             "Block comments nested too deeply (depth {depth})"
299:                         ),
300:                         severity: Severity::Error,
301:                         byte_range: byte_offset..byte_offset + line.len(),
302:                         line: line_idx + 1,
303:                         column: 1,
304:                         fix: None,
305:                     });
306:                 }
307:             } else if trimmed == "%}" {
308:                 depth = depth.saturating_sub(1);
309:             }
310:             byte_offset += line.len() + 1;
311:         }
312: 
313:         diagnostics
314:     }
315: }

    self.check_statement_depth(&metrics, source.len(), &mut diagnostics); // DEEPS

    // -- Line-based checks --

    diagnostics.extend(self.check_nested_block_comments(source)); // DEEPC

}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Verification for the incomplete_analysis split.

Checks:
  1. Each moved method body in the new files matches the original text
     (modulo indentation and the added `pub(crate)` qualifier).
  2. Each check ID's `rule_id: "X"` literal appears exactly once across
     the new directory.
  3. Every dispatch call in mod.rs's check_file has a matching definition.
  4. Moved-test count matches the original (28 tests total).
"""
import pathlib
import re
import sys

BASE = pathlib.Path("crates/mlt_rules/src/incomplete_analysis")
ORIG = pathlib.Path("crates/mlt_rules/src/incomplete_analysis.rs")

orig_text = ORIG.read_text()
new_files = sorted(BASE.rglob("*.rs"))
new_text = "\n".join(f.read_text() for f in new_files)


def strip_comment_markers(body: str) -> str:
    """Turn doc-comment marker `///` into plain `//` so `///` vs `//` does not
    matter for the body comparison."""
    lines = []
    for line in body.splitlines():
        stripped = line.lstrip()
        if stripped.startswith("///"):
            lines.append(line.replace("///", "//", 1))
        else:
            lines.append(line)
    return "\n".join(lines)


def normalize(body: str) -> str:
    body = strip_comment_markers(body)
    out = []
    for line in body.splitlines():
        s = line.strip()
        if not s:
            continue
        out.append(s)
    return "\n".join(out)


def extract_fn_body(text: str, marker: str) -> str:
    """Extract the body (between braces) of a fn whose signature line contains
    `marker`. Uses brace matching."""
    lines = text.splitlines()
    start = None
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if marker in line:
            start = i
            break
    assert start is not None, f"marker not found: {marker}"
    depth = 0
    found_open = False
    for i in range(start, len(lines)):
        for ch in lines[i]:
            if ch == "{":
                depth += 1
                found_open = True
            elif ch == "}":
                if found_open:
                    depth -= 1
                    if depth == 0:
                        return "\n".join(lines[start + 1 : i])
    raise AssertionError(f"no closing brace for marker: {marker}")


checks = [
    # (name, new-file, fn-marker-in-new-file, orig fn marker or None for inline)
    ("check_file_size", "check_file_size.rs", "fn check_file_size", None),
    ("check_extension", "check_extension.rs", "fn check_extension", None),
    ("check_node_count", "check_node_count.rs", "fn check_node_count", None),
    ("check_parse_errors", "check_parse_errors.rs", "fn check_parse_errors", None),
    ("check_nesting_depth", "check_nesting_depth.rs", "fn check_nesting_depth", None),
    ("check_paren_depth", "check_paren_depth.rs", "fn check_paren_depth", None),
    ("check_function_depth", "check_function_depth.rs", "fn check_function_depth", None),
    ("check_statement_depth", "check_statement_depth.rs", "fn check_statement_depth", None),
    ("check_incomplete_file", "check_incomplete_file.rs", "fn check_incomplete_file", None),
    ("check_line_lengths", "check_line_lengths.rs", "fn check_line_lengths", "fn check_line_lengths"),
    ("check_nested_block_comments", "check_block_comments.rs", "fn check_nested_block_comments", "fn check_nested_block_comments"),
    ("check_diagnostic_count", "check_diagnostic_count.rs", "fn check_diagnostic_count", None),
]

orig_normalized = normalize(orig_text)

print("=== 1. Moved method bodies match original (normalized substring search) ===")
failures = []
for name, fname, marker, orig_marker in checks:
    new_body = extract_fn_body((BASE / fname).read_text(), marker)
    new_norm = normalize(new_body)
    # In the new body, `pub(crate)` never appears (it is on the fn signature).
    if "pub(crate)" in new_norm:
        failures.append((name, "pub(crate) leaked into body"))
        continue
    if new_norm not in orig_normalized:
        failures.append((name, "normalized body NOT found in original"))
        continue
    print(f"  OK  {name}  (body matches original)")

# Also verify kept-in-mod.rs walker helpers match the original.
for name, marker in [("collect_metrics", "fn collect_metrics"), ("walk_tree", "fn walk_tree")]:
    new_body = extract_fn_body((BASE / "mod.rs").read_text(), marker)
    new_norm = normalize(new_body)
    if new_norm not in orig_normalized:
        failures.append((name, "normalized body NOT found in original"))
    else:
        print(f"  OK  {name}  (kept in mod.rs; body matches original)")

# last_descendant free fn.
last_desc = extract_fn_body((BASE / "mod.rs").read_text(), "fn last_descendant")
if normalize(last_desc) not in orig_normalized:
    failures.append(("last_descendant", "normalized body NOT found in original"))
else:
    print("  OK  last_descendant  (kept in mod.rs; body matches original)")

# Config struct: compare normalized IncompleteAnalysisConfig block + Default impl.
cfg_new = extract_fn_body((BASE / "mod.rs").read_text(), "struct IncompleteAnalysisConfig")
if normalize(cfg_new) not in orig_normalized:
    failures.append(("IncompleteAnalysisConfig", "normalized body NOT found in original"))
else:
    print("  OK  IncompleteAnalysisConfig  (kept in mod.rs; matches original)")

print("\n=== 2. Each check ID appears exactly once across the directory ===")
ids = sorted(
    set(re.findall(r'rule_id:\s*"([A-Z0-9_]+)"', new_text))
)
for cid in ids:
    count = len(re.findall(r'rule_id:\s*"%s"' % cid, new_text))
    status = "OK " if count == 1 else "FAIL"
    if count != 1:
        failures.append((f"rule_id {cid}", f"count = {count}"))
    print(f"  {status} {cid}: {count} occurrence(s)")
    if count != 1:
        print(f"       files: {[str(f) for f in new_files if cid in f.read_text()]}")

print("\n=== 3. Dispatch references match definitions ===")
mod_rs = (BASE / "mod.rs").read_text()
call_sites = sorted(set(re.findall(r"self\.(check_[a-z_]+)\(", mod_rs)))
def_sites = sorted(set(re.findall(r"pub\(crate\) fn (check_[a-z_]+)\(", new_text)))
print(f"  calls in check_file: {call_sites}")
print(f"  definitions:         {def_sites}")
if call_sites != def_sites:
    failures.append(("dispatch", f"calls {call_sites} != defs {def_sites}"))
else:
    print("  OK  dispatch calls match definitions exactly")

print("\n=== 4. Test counts ===")
orig_tests = len(re.findall(r"#\[test\]", orig_text))
new_tests = len(re.findall(r"#\[test\]", new_text))
print(f"  original tests: {orig_tests}")
print(f"  new tests:      {new_tests}")
if orig_tests != new_tests:
    failures.append(("test count", f"original {orig_tests} != new {new_tests}"))
else:
    print("  OK  test count preserved")

# Per-file test counts.
print("  per-file tests:")
for f in new_files:
    n = len(re.findall(r"#\[test\]", f.read_text()))
    print(f"    {f.relative_to(BASE)}: {n}")

# Moved test function names must be identical to the original test names.
orig_test_names = set(re.findall(r"fn (quit_[a-z_]+|mbig_[a-z_]+|textl_[a-z_]+|tmsms_[a-z_]+|eofer_[a-z_]+|eofmi_[a-z_]+|mxaset_[a-z_]+|nospc_[a-z_]+|mdeep_[a-z_]+|deepn_[a-z_]+|deepe_[a-z_]+|deeps_[a-z_]+|deepc_[a-z_]+|tmmsg_[a-z_]+)\(", orig_text))
new_test_names = set(re.findall(r"fn ([a-z_]+)\(", new_text))
missing = orig_test_names - new_test_names
extra = new_test_names - orig_test_names
print(f"  original test names not in new files: {sorted(missing) or 'none'}")
print(f"  new test names not in original:       {sorted(extra) or 'none'}")
if missing or extra:
    failures.append(("test names", f"missing={sorted(missing)} extra={sorted(extra)}"))

# Check no `use mlt_core::Config` needed in check files (helpers live in mod.rs)
print("\n=== 5. Shared test helpers referenced correctly ===")
for f in new_files:
    text = f.read_text()
    if "super::super" in text:
        refs = sorted(set(re.findall(r"use super::super::\{?([^;]+)", text)))
        print(f"  {f.name}: uses {refs}")
print("  mod.rs defines: engine, engine_with (cfg(test), pub(crate))")

print("\n" + ("!!! FAILURES: " + str(failures) if failures else "ALL CHECKS PASSED"))
sys.exit(1 if failures else 0)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Verification for the incomplete_analysis split (fixed extractor).

Checks:
  1. Each moved method body in the new files matches the original text
     (modulo indentation and the added `pub(crate)` qualifier).
  2. Each check ID's `rule_id: "X"` literal appears in exactly one file.
  3. Every dispatch call in mod.rs's check_file has a matching definition.
  4. Moved-test count matches the original (28 tests total) and all original
     test names are present.
"""
import pathlib
import re
import sys

BASE = pathlib.Path("crates/mlt_rules/src/incomplete_analysis")
ORIG = pathlib.Path("crates/mlt_rules/src/incomplete_analysis.rs")

orig_text = ORIG.read_text()
new_files = sorted(BASE.rglob("*.rs"))
new_text = "\n".join(f.read_text() for f in new_files)


def normalize(body: str) -> str:
    out = []
    for line in body.splitlines():
        s = line.strip()
        if not s:
            continue
        out.append(s)
    return "\n".join(out)


def extract_fn_body(text: str, marker: str) -> str:
    """Extract the body of a fn whose signature line contains `marker`.
    The body starts after the opening `{` and ends before the matching `}`."""
    lines = text.splitlines()
    start = None
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if marker in line:
            start = i
            break
    assert start is not None, f"marker not found: {marker}"
    depth = 0
    open_line = None
    for i in range(start, len(lines)):
        for ch in lines[i]:
            if ch == "{":
                depth += 1
                if open_line is None:
                    open_line = i
            elif ch == "}":
                depth -= 1
                if depth == 0 and open_line is not None:
                    return "\n".join(lines[open_line + 1 : i])
    raise AssertionError(f"no closing brace for marker: {marker}")


checks = [
    ("check_file_size", "check_file_size.rs", "fn check_file_size"),
    ("check_extension", "check_extension.rs", "fn check_extension"),
    ("check_node_count", "check_node_count.rs", "fn check_node_count"),
    ("check_parse_errors", "check_parse_errors.rs", "fn check_parse_errors"),
    ("check_nesting_depth", "check_nesting_depth.rs", "fn check_nesting_depth"),
    ("check_paren_depth", "check_paren_depth.rs", "fn check_paren_depth"),
    ("check_function_depth", "check_function_depth.rs", "fn check_function_depth"),
    ("check_statement_depth", "check_statement_depth.rs", "fn check_statement_depth"),
    ("check_incomplete_file", "check_incomplete_file.rs", "fn check_incomplete_file"),
    ("check_line_lengths", "check_line_lengths.rs", "fn check_line_lengths"),
    ("check_nested_block_comments", "check_block_comments.rs", "fn check_nested_block_comments"),
    ("check_diagnostic_count", "check_diagnostic_count.rs", "fn check_diagnostic_count"),
]

orig_normalized = normalize(orig_text)

print("=== 1. Moved method bodies match original (normalized substring search) ===")
failures = []
for name, fname, marker in checks:
    new_body = extract_fn_body((BASE / fname).read_text(), marker)
    new_norm = normalize(new_body)
    if "pub(crate)" in new_norm:
        failures.append((name, "pub(crate) leaked into body"))
        print(f"  FAIL {name}: pub(crate) leaked into body")
        continue
    if new_norm not in orig_normalized:
        failures.append((name, "normalized body NOT found in original"))
        print(f"  FAIL {name}: normalized body NOT found in original")
        continue
    print(f"  OK  {name}")

# Kept-in-mod.rs walker helpers + free helper + config.
for name, marker in [("collect_metrics", "fn collect_metrics"), ("walk_tree", "fn walk_tree")]:
    body = normalize(extract_fn_body((BASE / "mod.rs").read_text(), marker))
    if body not in orig_normalized:
        failures.append((name, "normalized body NOT found in original"))
        print(f"  FAIL {name}: normalized body NOT found in original")
    else:
        print(f"  OK  {name} (kept in mod.rs)")

last_desc = normalize(extract_fn_body((BASE / "mod.rs").read_text(), "fn last_descendant"))
if last_desc not in orig_normalized:
    failures.append(("last_descendant", "normalized body NOT found in original"))
    print("  FAIL last_descendant")
else:
    print("  OK  last_descendant (kept in mod.rs)")

cfg = normalize(extract_fn_body((BASE / "mod.rs").read_text(), "struct IncompleteAnalysisConfig"))
if cfg not in orig_normalized:
    failures.append(("IncompleteAnalysisConfig", "normalized body NOT found in original"))
    print("  FAIL IncompleteAnalysisConfig")
else:
    print("  OK  IncompleteAnalysisConfig (kept in mod.rs)")

print("\n=== 2. Each check ID appears in exactly one file ===")
all_ids = sorted(set(re.findall(r'rule_id:\s*"([A-Z0-9_]+)"', new_text)))
for cid in all_ids:
    files_with = [f.name for f in new_files if re.search(r'rule_id:\s*"%s"' % cid, f.read_text())]
    occ = len(re.findall(r'rule_id:\s*"%s"' % cid, new_text))
    status = "OK " if len(files_with) == 1 else "FAIL"
    if len(files_with) != 1:
        failures.append((f"rule_id {cid}", f"files={files_with}"))
    print(f"  {status} {cid}: {occ} literal(s) in {files_with}")

print("\n=== 3. Dispatch references match definitions ===")
mod_rs = (BASE / "mod.rs").read_text()
call_sites = sorted(set(re.findall(r"self\.(check_[a-z_]+)\(", mod_rs)))
def_sites = sorted(set(re.findall(r"pub\(crate\) fn (check_[a-z_]+)\(", new_text)))
print(f"  calls: {call_sites}")
print(f"  defs:  {def_sites}")
if call_sites != def_sites:
    failures.append(("dispatch", f"calls {call_sites} != defs {def_sites}"))
else:
    print("  OK  dispatch calls match definitions exactly")

print("\n=== 4. Test counts and names ===")
orig_tests = len(re.findall(r"#\[test\]", orig_text))
new_tests = len(re.findall(r"#\[test\]", new_text))
print(f"  original tests: {orig_tests}, new tests: {new_tests}")
if orig_tests != new_tests:
    failures.append(("test count", f"original {orig_tests} != new {new_tests}"))
else:
    print("  OK  test count preserved")
for f in new_files:
    n = len(re.findall(r"#\[test\]", f.read_text()))
    print(f"    {f.name}: {n}")

# Compare only #[test] fn names.
def test_fns(text):
    out = []
    for m in re.finditer(r"#\[test\]\s*\n\s*fn\s+([a-z_0-9]+)\s*\(", text):
        out.append(m.group(1))
    return out

orig_names = sorted(set(test_fns(orig_text)))
new_names = sorted(set(test_fns(new_text)))
missing = [n for n in orig_names if n not in new_names]
extra = [n for n in new_names if n not in orig_names]
print(f"  original test fns not in new files: {missing or 'none'}")
print(f"  new test fns not in original:       {extra or 'none'}")
if missing or extra:
    failures.append(("test names", f"missing={missing} extra={extra}"))

print("\n=== 5. Shared test helpers ===")
for f in new_files:
    if f.name == "mod.rs":
        continue
    text = f.read_text()
    refs = sorted(set(re.findall(r"use super::super::\{\s*([^}]+)\s*\}", text)) | set(re.findall(r"use super::super::([a-z_]+);", text)))
    print(f"  {f.name}: {refs}")

print("\n" + ("!!! FAILURES: " + str(failures) if failures else "ALL CHECKS PASSED"))
sys.exit(1 if failures else 0)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Rigorous dedent-based line diff of every moved body + the check_file dispatch."""
import difflib
import pathlib

BASE = pathlib.Path("crates/mlt_rules/src/incomplete_analysis")
ORIG = pathlib.Path("crates/mlt_rules/src/incomplete_analysis.rs")
orig_text = ORIG.read_text()
orig_lines = orig_text.splitlines()


def dedent(text: str) -> list[str]:
    lines = text.splitlines()
    if not lines:
        return []
    margin = None
    for ln in lines:
        stripped = ln.lstrip()
        if not stripped:
            continue
        m = len(ln) - len(stripped)
        margin = m if margin is None else min(margin, m)
    if margin is None:
        margin = 0
    return [ln[margin:] if len(ln) >= margin else ln for ln in lines]


def extract_fn_body(text: str, marker: str) -> str:
    lines = text.splitlines()
    start = next(i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if marker in l)
    depth = 0
    open_line = None
    for i in range(start, len(lines)):
        for ch in lines[i]:
            if ch == "{":
                depth += 1
                if open_line is None:
                    open_line = i
            elif ch == "}":
                depth -= 1
                if depth == 0 and open_line is not None:
                    return "\n".join(lines[open_line + 1 : i])
    raise AssertionError(marker)


def extract_block(text: str, start_marker: str, end_before_marker: str) -> str:
    """Extract original inline block: from line containing start_marker up to
    (not including) the line containing end_before_marker."""
    lines = text.splitlines()
    s = next(i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if start_marker in l)
    e = next(i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if end_before_marker in l)
    assert s < e, (start_marker, end_before_marker)
    return "\n".join(lines[s:e])


def show(name: str, orig_block: str, new_block: str) -> None:
    a = dedent(orig_block)
    b = dedent(new_block)
    if a == b:
        print(f"OK   {name}: byte-identical after dedent ({len(a)} lines)")
        return
    print(f"DIFF {name}:")
    diff = list(difflib.unified_diff(a, b, "original", "new", lineterm=""))
    for line in diff[:60]:
        print("    " + line)
    print()


orig_check_file = extract_fn_body(orig_text, "fn check_file")
new_check_file = extract_fn_body((BASE / "mod.rs").read_text(), "fn check_file")
show("check_file (dispatch)", orig_check_file, new_check_file)

# Per-method diffs (original side = inline block; new side = method body).
new_by_name = {
    "check_file_size": extract_fn_body((BASE / "check_file_size.rs").read_text(), "fn check_file_size"),
    "check_extension": extract_fn_body((BASE / "check_extension.rs").read_text(), "fn check_extension"),
    "check_node_count": extract_fn_body((BASE / "check_node_count.rs").read_text(), "fn check_node_count"),
    "check_parse_errors": extract_fn_body((BASE / "check_parse_errors.rs").read_text(), "fn check_parse_errors"),
    "check_nesting_depth": extract_fn_body((BASE / "check_nesting_depth.rs").read_text(), "fn check_nesting_depth"),
    "check_paren_depth": extract_fn_body((BASE / "check_paren_depth.rs").read_text(), "fn check_paren_depth"),
    "check_function_depth": extract_fn_body((BASE / "check_function_depth.rs").read_text(), "fn check_function_depth"),
    "check_statement_depth": extract_fn_body((BASE / "check_statement_depth.rs").read_text(), "fn check_statement_depth"),
    "check_incomplete_file": extract_fn_body((BASE / "check_incomplete_file.rs").read_text(), "fn check_incomplete_file"),
    "check_line_lengths": extract_fn_body((BASE / "check_line_lengths.rs").read_text(), "fn check_line_lengths"),
    "check_nested_block_comments": extract_fn_body((BASE / "check_block_comments.rs").read_text(), "fn check_nested_block_comments"),
    "check_diagnostic_count": extract_fn_body((BASE / "check_diagnostic_count.rs").read_text(), "fn check_diagnostic_count"),
}

orig_blocks = {
    "check_file_size": ("if source.len() > self.config.max_file_size {", "// MDOTM: Invalid file extension"),
    "check_extension": ("if let Some(ext) = ctx.file_path.extension() {", "// -- Single-pass tree traversal --"),
    "check_node_count": ("if metrics.node_count > self.config.max_node_count {", "// TMSMS: Too many parse errors."),
    "check_parse_errors": ("// TMSMS: Too many parse errors.", "// NOSPC: File too complex (nesting)"),
    "check_nesting_depth": ("// NOSPC: File too complex (nesting)", "// MDEEP: Parentheses/brackets nested too deeply."),
    "check_paren_depth": ("if metrics.max_paren_depth > self.config.max_paren_depth {", "// DEEPN: Functions nested too deeply."),
    "check_function_depth": ("if metrics.max_function_depth > self.config.max_function_depth {", "// DEEPS: Statements nested too deeply."),

    show(name, orig_body, new_body)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Verification for the incomplete_analysis split (unique path to avoid
collision with parallel pipeline runs)."""
import pathlib
import re
import sys

BASE = pathlib.Path("crates/mlt_rules/src/incomplete_analysis")
ORIG = pathlib.Path("crates/mlt_rules/src/incomplete_analysis.rs")

orig_text = ORIG.read_text()
new_files = sorted(BASE.rglob("*.rs"))
new_text = "\n".join(f.read_text() for f in new_files)


def normalize(body: str) -> str:
    out = []
    for line in body.splitlines():
        s = line.strip()
        if not s:
            continue
        out.append(s)
    return "\n".join(out)


def extract_fn_body(text: str, marker: str) -> str:
    lines = text.splitlines()
    start = next(i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if marker in l)
    depth = 0
    open_line = None
    for i in range(start, len(lines)):
        for ch in lines[i]:
            if ch == "{":
                depth += 1
                if open_line is None:
                    open_line = i
            elif ch == "}":
                depth -= 1
                if depth == 0 and open_line is not None:
                    return "\n".join(lines[open_line + 1 : i])
    raise AssertionError(marker)


checks = [
    ("check_file_size", "check_file_size.rs", "fn check_file_size"),
    ("check_extension", "check_extension.rs", "fn check_extension"),
    ("check_node_count", "check_node_count.rs", "fn check_node_count"),
    ("check_parse_errors", "check_parse_errors.rs", "fn check_parse_errors"),
    ("check_nesting_depth", "check_nesting_depth.rs", "fn check_nesting_depth"),
    ("check_paren_depth", "check_paren_depth.rs", "fn check_paren_depth"),
    ("check_function_depth", "check_function_depth.rs", "fn check_function_depth"),
    ("check_statement_depth", "check_statement_depth.rs", "fn check_statement_depth"),
    ("check_incomplete_file", "check_incomplete_file.rs", "fn check_incomplete_file"),
    ("check_line_lengths", "check_line_lengths.rs", "fn check_line_lengths"),
    ("check_nested_block_comments", "check_block_comments.rs", "fn check_nested_block_comments"),
    ("check_diagnostic_count", "check_diagnostic_count.rs", "fn check_diagnostic_count"),
]

orig_normalized = normalize(orig_text)

print("=== 1. Moved method bodies match original (normalized substring search) ===")
failures = []
for name, fname, marker in checks:
    new_body = extract_fn_body((BASE / fname).read_text(), marker)
    new_norm = normalize(new_body)
    if "pub(crate)" in new_norm:
        failures.append((name, "pub(crate) leaked into body"))
        print(f"  FAIL {name}: pub(crate) leaked into body")
        continue
    if new_norm not in orig_normalized:
        failures.append((name, "normalized body NOT found in original"))
        print(f"  FAIL {name}: normalized body NOT found in original")
        continue
    print(f"  OK  {name}")

for name, marker in [("collect_metrics", "fn collect_metrics"), ("walk_tree", "fn walk_tree")]:
    body = normalize(extract_fn_body((BASE / "mod.rs").read_text(), marker))
    if body not in orig_normalized:
        failures.append((name, "normalized body NOT found in original"))
        print(f"  FAIL {name}: normalized body NOT found in original")
    else:
        print(f"  OK  {name} (kept in mod.rs)")

last_desc = normalize(extract_fn_body((BASE / "mod.rs").read_text(), "fn last_descendant"))
if last_desc not in orig_normalized:
    failures.append(("last_descendant", "normalized body NOT found in original"))
    print("  FAIL last_descendant")
else:
    print("  OK  last_descendant (kept in mod.rs)")

cfg = normalize(extract_fn_body((BASE / "mod.rs").read_text(), "struct IncompleteAnalysisConfig"))
if cfg not in orig_normalized:
    failures.append(("IncompleteAnalysisConfig", "normalized body NOT found in original"))
    print("  FAIL IncompleteAnalysisConfig")
else:
    print("  OK  IncompleteAnalysisConfig (kept in mod.rs)")

print("\n=== 2. Each check ID appears in exactly one file ===")
all_ids = sorted(set(re.findall(r'rule_id:\s*"([A-Z0-9_]+)"', new_text)))
for cid in all_ids:
    files_with = [f.name for f in new_files if re.search(r'rule_id:\s*"%s"' % cid, f.read_text())]
    occ = len(re.findall(r'rule_id:\s*"%s"' % cid, new_text))
    status = "OK " if len(files_with) == 1 else "FAIL"
    if len(files_with) != 1:
        failures.append((f"rule_id {cid}", f"files={files_with}"))
    print(f"  {status} {cid}: {occ} literal(s) in {files_with}")

print("\n=== 3. Dispatch references match definitions ===")
mod_rs = (BASE / "mod.rs").read_text()
call_sites = sorted(set(re.findall(r"self\.(check_[a-z_]+)\(", mod_rs)))
def_sites = sorted(set(re.findall(r"pub\(crate\) fn (check_[a-z_]+)\(", new_text)))
print(f"  calls: {call_sites}")
print(f"  defs:  {def_sites}")
if call_sites != def_sites:
    failures.append(("dispatch", f"calls {call_sites} != defs {def_sites}"))
else:
    print("  OK  dispatch calls match definitions exactly")

print("\n=== 4. Test counts and names ===")
orig_tests = len(re.findall(r"#\[test\]", orig_text))
new_tests = len(re.findall(r"#\[test\]", new_text))
print(f"  original tests: {orig_tests}, new tests: {new_tests}")
if orig_tests != new_tests:
    failures.append(("test count", f"original {orig_tests} != new {new_tests}"))
else:
    print("  OK  test count preserved")
for f in new_files:
    n = len(re.findall(r"#\[test\]", f.read_text()))
    print(f"    {f.name}: {n}")


def test_fns(text):
    return sorted(set(re.findall(r"#\[test\]\s*\n\s*fn\s+([a-z_0-9]+)\s*\(", text)))


orig_names = test_fns(orig_text)
new_names = test_fns(new_text)
missing = [n for n in orig_names if n not in new_names]
extra = [n for n in new_names if n not in orig_names]
print(f"  original test fns not in new files: {missing or 'none'}")
print(f"  new test fns not in original:       {extra or 'none'}")
if missing or extra:
    failures.append(("test names", f"missing={missing} extra={extra}"))

print("\n" + ("!!! FAILURES: " + str(failures) if failures else "ALL CHECKS PASSED"))
